newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan voices protest at India jet "intrusion".
newsitem.headline: Pakistan voices protest at India jet "intrusion".

text.p: Pakistan lodged a strong protest with India on Wednesday against what it said was a violation of its airspace by an Indian jet fighter, which also set off shock waves that rattled windows in Islamabad.

A government statement said India's acting High Commissioner (ambassador) was called to the Foreign Ministry and told of Pakistan's "serious concern...at this intrusion" on Tuesday, which it said violated international law and a bilateral agreement on preventing airspace violations.
"He was told that the government of India should take immediate measures to ensure that such violations of Pakistan airspace by Indian aircraft do not recur," it said.
The incident, denied by an Indian Defence Ministry spokesman, also echoed in the Pakistani parliament reviving talk of rivalry between the two old enemies after a recent resumption of peace talks.
Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan, speaking in the National Assembly, called the alleged violation serious and said it could have been made to photograph strategic installations.
But he said Pakistan did not have missiles that can shoot at the height taken by the Indian jet, which a Pakistan Air Force (PAF) saapokesman said was more than 60,000 feet (18,288 metres).
A PAF statement said a loud boom that shook windows of buildings in Islamabad was caused by the Indian jet when it broke the sound barrier while flying out of Pakistan airspace.

"The intruding aircraft was tracked by the PAF radar network and defensive measures were immediately ordered," it said. "The violator, because of high altitude and speed, exited prior to retaliatory action."
A defence ministry spokesman in New Delhi denied the aircraft was Indian, the United News of India said.
"No Indian aircraft has crossed the international border," the news agency quoted the spokesman as saying.
Indian Defence Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment. An Indian Foreign Ministry spokesman earlier said he had no information about the incident.

The PAF charged that the entry of the Indian jet, possibly an air force MiG-25R flying at twice the speed of sound, was presumed to have been either an intentional high speed reconnaissance run or an accidental violation.

It said the plane had entered Pakistan airspace from a control line dividing the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir near the border city of Sialkot and flew along the international boundary, exiting the control line near Poonch in Kashmir.
A police official in Rawalpindi, near Islamabad, had told Reuters on Tuesday that the explosion heard in the capital was probably caused by a construction company levelling ground.
